note: Values copied from the project's saved evaluation files (artifacts/model/*.csv). Nothing here was re-run by the agent.

training.feature_set: extended (12 sensors, rolling mean/std over 5 and 10 observations, rolling mean over 20, EWM, offset from early level, cycle)
training.target_policy: uncapped RUL in operating cycles; models predict sqrt(RUL); predictions squared and clipped at 0

test_endpoint.split: 100 official test engines, final observed cycle of each (truncated histories)

test_all_cycles.split: every observed row of the 100 test engines

test_endpoint_by_true_rul_band.note: Bands use the TRUE RUL, which is unknown for a live engine, so they cannot adjust an individual estimate.

model_agreement.note: Exploratory, 100 test endpoints. Uncalibrated heuristic, not a confidence interval.

limitations: Simulated FD001 data (one operating condition, one fault mode); results do not transfer to other conditions without new evaluation.
Predictions are in operating cycles and cannot be converted to calendar time without a usage assumption.
Typical error at an arbitrary cutoff is about 30 cycles (MAE across all test rows); the 14 to 15 cycle endpoint MAE applies only to the final observed cycle of truncated test engines.
Overestimation is the risky direction and was most common when much life remained; several of the largest endpoint errors were overestimates for engines with only 31 to 72 observed cycles.
Engines among the 70 training engines are in-sample, so their estimates are optimistic.
The point estimate has no uncertainty interval; the model-agreement gap is an uncalibrated heuristic.
The estimate need not decrease steadily as new cycles arrive.
The system holds no maintenance procedures, repair actions or part-level diagnoses and cannot give them.
